screens.name: Broadcast Preview
screens.rail: none; main takes the rail's column from 1024px (data-rail="none")
screens.firstViewport: Title and verdict naming who holds items; match keys and partner keys; the program monitor at full width; the rundown beneath, beside it from 1800px (minmax(0,1fr) minmax(44rem,1fr)) with the monitor sticky.
screens.keyboard: 1/2/3 partner on the monitor; G safe areas; Esc back to program. Ignored in fields and with Alt, Ctrl or Meta.
screens.phone: At 720px and below: partner keys become a three-up grid reading cap and code; the monitor bar hides the locale; rundown rows become cards labelled by partner code; the table keeps explicit roles.

screens.name: Approvals
screens.rail: none; main takes the rail's column from 1024px (data-rail="none")
screens.firstViewport: Title and verdict naming how many wait and since which match minute; match keys; a polite message line (height reserved) naming the item just decided; the floor: the call sheet of waiting tickets at the left (18rem | 1fr from 1280px, stacking above the desk below) with K/J beside the 'Waiting' heading only when 2+ wait; the desk (7fr | 5fr from 1280px): the item on its partner's stage (the program monitor in preview, no guides, its own stageLabel), 'In English' (the English partner's version) or 'As written', 'Why it waits' (policy reason, evidence count, checked twice; a red-lamp line when a correction has since changed its facts), the A and R keys, the duty-editor (demo identity) line, the reject form; the decisions log beneath. Empty floor (data-empty): the call sheet spans the floor.

verdict.idle: This match has not started. Start the matchday from Match Live. (neutral)
verdict.running: N items wait for an editor; the oldest since 61'. (amber) / Nothing waits for an editor. N decisions this match. (green once decided, else neutral)
verdict.finished: Full time. N held items stayed off air. / Full time. Nothing waits for an editor; N decisions this match. (neutral)
verdict.failed: This match's replay stopped. Held items stay off air. (red)
verdict.unavailable: The match service is unavailable. Retrying every few seconds. (red)

screens.keyboard: A approve; R reject (opens a one-line reason, prefilled 'A correction changed this item's facts' for a corrected item); Esc cancel (visible Esc cap on Cancel); J/K next/previous. Ignored on key repeat, with Shift, Alt, Ctrl or Meta, during IME composition and while typing; the keystroke is consumed by the shortcut. E (edit and approve) is not offered.
screens.safety: After the desk shows a different item, keys and buttons wait 600ms (settle); also while a request is in flight, outside a running match and before the run is known. An item decided here leaves the queue at once. When the item on the desk is decided elsewhere, the desk keeps its place, shows the item that took it and the message line says so. A corrected item can only be rejected.
screens.focus: After a decision, the new item's desk heading; after Cancel, the R key; the 'Waiting' heading when the queue empties.
screens.phone: At 720px and below the decisions log becomes cards of labelled lines; the table keeps explicit roles.

components.name: Program Monitor
components.description: Broadcast Preview: a bar (Program/Preview tally, partner, LED clock) over a 16:9 stage authored at 1920x1080 (--u = 100cqw/1920) on a placeholder pitch, no video. Graphics in the partner's own look and Barlow Condensed: lower third with the policy's exact disclosure label, correction strap preempting it, score bug on the match clock in program. Safe areas: action 90% dashed, title 80% dotted; they differ by dash pattern, not hue. An optional stageLabel replaces the stage's default spoken label (the Approvals desk uses it to say the words are on the desk as text).

components.name: Ticket
components.description: Approvals: one call-sheet entry, oldest first. Head line of 11px uppercase labels: partner code ink-1, kind icon and label ink-3, and at the right the minute it has waited since in amber (waiting is a state); the partner's words beneath in 13px ink-2 in their own lang. Current (aria-current): panel-2, strong hairline edge, 2px board-white inset rule, ink-1.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Fourth Official's Board"**

The control room speaks the fourth official's language: the LED substitution board. Lit 5x7 dot-matrix numerals sit on a black panel field, and state is the board's red, green and amber light. Everything else is anodised near-black hardware: panels joined by hairlines, square-cut keys, round lamps, silk-screened uppercase labels. It is built for a dark production gallery at 1440 to 1920 wide, read in glances between other monitors.

Density is high but ordered. Each screen leads with one verdict line an executive can read in five seconds, then a wall of match boards an operator scans for lamps, tallies and counts. Colour is never decoration: it appears only as signal light, so a lit dot always means something.

The system refuses the generic dark SaaS dashboard: rounded-card soup, glowing charts, gradients, coloured accents used for brand or emphasis.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black anodised panels, flat, joined by 1px hairlines.
5x7 dot-matrix LED readouts with faint unlit dots for scorelines and clocks.
Colour only as signal light: one colour, one icon and one label per state.
Geist for UI text with tabular figures; Geist Mono only on key caps; Barlow Condensed only inside the Broadcast Preview monitor.

rules.name: The Signal Light Rule
rules.body: Colour appears only as signal light. Green, red, amber and violet mean item or system state; if nothing has that state, the colour is absent. Never use them for brand, emphasis, charts or links.

rules.name: The State Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: Each item state has exactly one colour, one icon and one label, identical on every screen, and is never shown by colour alone:

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue is reserved for the AI tag. Nothing else is blue.

rules.name: The White Clock Rule
rules.body: Clocks and scorelines are lit white. A number becomes a state colour only when it is itself a state (a pending count, an SLO breach).

rules.name: The Silk-screen Rule
rules.body: Uppercase only at 11px with 0.08em tracking, and only for hardware labels. Sentence case everywhere else.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: Lit things are lit by colour, not by blur or bloom. No glow shadows, no gradients behind readouts or charts. The one sanctioned exception is the lit tally lamp's small specular highlight (a radial gradient from #ff8a80 into led-red), which models a physical bulb.

rules.name: The One Moment Rule
rules.body: This is the single authored motion moment: the IN panel's lit dots light up 260ms after OUT, over 420ms ease-out, like the board being raised. No other element animates for effect.

rules.name: The Stage Rule
rules.body: Partner colours live inside the monitor's stage only, never in the chrome. Around the frame the board's palette and signal lights apply unchanged; inside it, no partner colour means state.

dos: **Do** use one colour, one icon and one label per item state, exactly as in the State Vocabulary table.
**Do** keep clocks and scorelines lit white; set numbers in tabular figures.
**Do** draw LED readouts with 5x7 glyphs, a 1-dot gap, whole-pixel dot sizes, fixed character width and faint unlit dots.
**Do** give the featured match the largest board on the wall.
**Do** summarise every correction with the OUT/IN board.
**Do** lead every screen with a verdict line.
**Do** use the 2px key radius for hardware and perfect circles for lamps.
**Do** show the focus ring (2px gallery-black gap, 2px board-white ring) on every focusable element.
**Do** honour `prefers-reduced-motion`: all animation and transition durations collapse to 0.01ms (Match Live also stops the verifying spinner and the provenance chevron's rotation outright).
**Do** label replay mode, synthetic data and AI content.
**Do** keep what went out visible: strike retracted text in red, and keep amended claims struck in violet under "As published".
**Do** let a key's label carry its state (Starting…, Matchday running, Ready in m:ss) rather than hiding why it is disabled.
**Do** give every keyboard shortcut a visible key cap and `aria-keyshortcuts`.
**Do** keep a text equivalent beside every picture of a broadcast: the rundown lists everything the monitor shows.
**Do** name the duty editor as a demo identity wherever a decision names an editor; this demo has no sign-in.
**Do** keep an editor's keys waiting until the item on the desk has been seen: never let a decision land on an item the editor has not had time to read.
donts: **Don't** add glow, bloom or drop shadows, and don't use gradients (the tally lamp highlight is the only exception).
**Don't** build rounded-card soup: no radius above 2px on containers, no floating cards.
**Don't** use green, amber, red or violet for anything that is not a state; don't use blue for anything but the AI tag.
**Don't** colour a clock or scoreline by state.

**Don't** add motion beyond the OUT/IN light-up and state transitions of 160 to 220ms (the functional exceptions are loading spinners, the disclosure chevron, and broadcast graphics animating in within 360ms inside the monitor, as they do on air).
**Don't** use partner or tenant brand colours or the graphics face in the chrome; they belong only inside the Broadcast Preview monitor's stage.
**Don't** mark moment kinds with colour; a kind is an icon and a label.
**Don't** repeat a correction's state with a lamp when its strap already names it.
